reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes an Ethereum trading bot as an easy source of daily passive income and claims a return of more than 31% after roughly 12 hours. It instructs viewers to deploy the contract, transfer at least 0.5 ETH to its address, and increase the deposit to pursue larger transactions and more profit. The video describes a sandwich-trading mechanism, but the reported profits are not established as genuine or reproducible.

citations.quote: Today I'll be teaching you step by step how to deploy an Ethereum trading bot I've recently developed in the Solidity language which can make you a very easy daily passive income.
Deposit funds (at least 0.5 ETH to prevent negating slippage) to your exact contract/bot address

You can fund a contract with whatever amount of Ethereum you want but obviously, the more you put in, the larger the transaction you will be able to sandwich and the more profit you will be able to accumulate over time
The amount we funded the contract with is 1 ETH.
So as you can see, I have about 1.31 Ethereum is more than 31% profit already.

opening.argument: The presentation does not promise a fixed or guaranteed return. It expressly says that results vary over time, while also identifying operational costs and token-fee conditions that can reduce performance. That is materially different from representing profit as certain: the audience is told that “the profits will fluctuate week to week,” and the description discusses gas fees and possible burn fees. The content therefore reads as a conditional technical demonstration with disclosed risks, not a categorical assurance that every user will profit.

citations.quote: the profits will fluctuate week to week
I've received messages from people who didn't fund the contract with enough Ethereum to cover gas fees and possible burn fees.
If you fund the contract with 0.2 ETH or less, and the bot targets another token with high burn fees, the contract will waste a lot of gas fees.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing account emphasizes promotional language and one reported result, but those statements do not establish that the result was fabricated or that a return was guaranteed. The same material expressly qualifies outcomes as variable and identifies circumstances in which costs can consume funds. A claim of personal performance, even if optimistic, is not by itself proof of deceptive intent.

citations.quote: the profits will fluctuate week to week
The bot targets token contracts with max 10% burn fee and anything lower.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The qualifications describe costs and variability, but they do not withdraw the central inducement. The speaker still presents the system as easy daily passive income and reports substantial gains after operation. Warning that results fluctuate can make an earnings pitch sound more credible without showing that ordinary viewers can reproduce it.

citations.quote: which can make you a very easy daily passive income
i've even had weeks where i've made three to six, Ethereum sometimes more

opening.argument: The primary activity is a programming and blockchain operations tutorial. The speaker explains a Solidity contract, directs viewers through Remix, compiler settings, deployment, and contract controls, and emphasizes that no coding experience is required. Those are concrete instructional steps for using a development tool, not merely a request to send money to an opaque operator. The sampled visuals are consistent with that technical workflow: source code is shown in an editor and the Remix deployment interface is visible.

citations.quote: Today I'll be teaching you step by step how to deploy an Ethereum trading bot I've recently developed in the Solidity language
And you don't need any coding experience whatsoever.
Under Compiler select the 0.6.6 version so that it matches our contract.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the material promotional does not eliminate its substantial technical content. The video explains the mempool and transaction ordering, shows compilation and deployment, and identifies the contract controls. Even if the speaker also describes personal results, the observable format remains an operational tutorial that teaches viewers how the tool is constructed and used.

citations.quote: it sniffs the mempool for transactions that are pending within a block
Now we are going to deploy this to our wallet.
Now you can see the 4 actions for our smart contract

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Technical instructions can be the delivery mechanism for a financial solicitation. Here, the tutorial does not stop at explaining Solidity: it instructs viewers to fund the deployed contract, start it, and pursue larger profits. The coding detail therefore supports implementation of the promoted earning scheme rather than independently establishing an educational purpose.

citations.quote: the next step is to fund the contract with some Ethereum to snipe liquidity pools
Last step is to click start.
Deposit funds (at least 0.5 ETH to prevent negating slippage) to your exact contract/bot address

opening.argument: The material describes a user-operated software tool and its transaction mechanics, not a conventional scam structure involving account credentials, recruitment, or downline payments. The instructions direct users to deploy their own contract through Remix and MetaMask, and the described interaction includes a withdrawal function that returns funds to the wallet. The supplied evidence does not show a request for a password, private key, or payment to an intermediary. That makes the content more plausibly an ordinary technical service or self-directed blockchain activity, even if its profitability claims deserve independent verification.

citations.quote: the bot, which I like to refer to as a slippage bot, allows you to automatic trade a given token from the Ethereum blockchain
Now we are going to deploy this to our wallet.
Withdraw, stops the bot and transfers the funds back into your wallet

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing account treats funding as proof of a scam mechanism, but funding a smart contract is also a normal part of operating the described tool. The material identifies deployment, gas fees, contract actions, and withdrawal, rather than showing credential harvesting or recruitment. The fact that a financial activity involves risk does not by itself establish that it is fraudulent.

citations.quote: We need to confirm the contract on the blockchain by paying Gas Fees.
Withdraw, stops the bot and transfers the funds back into your wallet.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of password collection or recruitment does not resolve the core issue. The material specifically directs viewers to transfer Ether to a contract address and presents the contract as generating passive income. A withdrawal button and visible deployment steps show an operational interface, but they do not prove that deposited funds will be returned or that the claimed trading activity actually produced the reported gains.
